conventions.convention: FI has all finite sets as objects and injections as morphisms; [n]={0,…,n−1}, including [0]=∅. FI-modules are covariant functors to unital left modules over a commutative ring.
Finite generation means generation by finitely many elements globally. Generation in degree ≤d means generation by all skeletal values in degrees ≤d and does not require pointwise finite generation.

Φₐ(V)ₙ takes Sₙ-coinvariants of V on a fixed a-element block disjoint from a moving n-element block. T fixes the a-block, adds one moving point, and is Sₐ-equivariant. Φₐ is right exact generally and exact when the coefficient ring contains Q.
Injectivity and surjectivity thresholds concern the moving degree n, uniformly for every a≥0. Stability degree is their maximum; thresholds may be infinite.
Over every characteristic-zero field, Specht modules are obtained from rational models and classify all simple symmetric-group modules. No scalar extension from C to an arbitrary field is assumed.
λ[n]=(n−|λ|,λ₁,λ₂,…) is defined exactly for n≥|λ|+λ₁. For the empty partition, |λ|=λ₁=0 and λ[0]=∅.

A constituent is a simple subquotient, without a finite-dimensionality requirement on the ambient value. Weight is the supremum of padding-tail sizes, is zero for the zero module, and decreases under subquotients.

Uniform representation stability requires finite-dimensional values, injective transition maps, generation of the next value by the symmetric-group span of the image, and simultaneous constancy of all padded multiplicities. Multiplicities are set to zero below their padding thresholds.
Character polynomials have rational coefficients, finitely many monomials, and weighted degree deg Xᵢ=i. Agreement on infinitely many symmetric-group ranks determines the polynomial uniquely.

In the exterior-square example, the integer-valued cycle-count expression is evaluated over the integers before mapping to k; this includes characteristic 2 without reducing rational coefficients individually.

load_bearing.statement: Φₐ(V)ₙ=(V on the disjoint a- and n-element blocks)_{Sₙ}; T is independent of the chosen injection of the moving block and is Sₐ-equivariant. Φₐ is right exact, and exact when k contains Q.

For a field F of characteristic 0 and n≥0, the nonzero Specht modules S^λ_F, λ⊢n, form a complete irredundant list of irreducible FSₙ-modules; every finite-dimensional FSₙ-module is a direct sum of copies of these modules.

Over a characteristic-zero field, induction of S^λ_F⊠F from Sₙ×Sₖ to Sₙ₊ₖ is the multiplicity-one sum over horizontal k-strip additions. For 0≤k≤n, Sₖ-coinvariants of its restriction to Sₙ₋ₖ×Sₖ are the multiplicity-one sum over horizontal k-strip removals.

V is finitely generated iff it is a quotient of a finite sum of M(mᵢ). V is generated in degree ≤d iff it is a quotient of a possibly infinite sum of M(mᵢ) with all mᵢ≤d. Finite generation implies pointwise finite generation.
inj-deg(M(W))=0; if Wᵢ=0 for i>m, then surj-deg(M(W))≤m. Over a nonzero ring, stab-deg(M(m))=m. Over a characteristic-zero field, weight(M(λ))=|λ| and stab-deg(M(λ))=λ₁.
Quotients do not increase surjectivity degree. Generation in degree ≤d implies surjectivity degree ≤d over any coefficient ring, and weight ≤d over a characteristic-zero field.

For a characteristic-zero field and padded irreducible V(λ)ₙ, its Sₙ₋ₐ-coinvariants vanish iff a<|λ|, equal V_λ when a=|λ|, and equal Ind_{S_|λ|×Sₐ₋|λ|}^{Sₐ}(V_λ⊠k) when a≥|λ| and n≥a+λ₁. If weight(V)≤a, then every subquotient Wₙ of Vₙ, n≥a, vanishes iff its Sₙ₋ₐ-coinvariants vanish.
If k is a commutative Noetherian ring containing Q and V is a finitely generated FI-module over k, then every sub-FI-module W⊆V is finitely generated.
For an FI-module V over a characteristic-zero field with finite stability degree s, every constituent V(λ)ₙ of every Vₙ satisfies λ₁≤s; this bounds the second row of λ[n].
An FI-module over a characteristic-zero field with finite-dimensional values, finite weight d and finite stability degree s is uniformly representation stable in the range n≥d+s.
For an FI-module V over a characteristic-zero field with finite-dimensional values, V is finitely generated iff its associated consistent sequence is uniformly representation stable.

Over a characteristic-zero field, for d=|λ|+λ₁ there is a sub-FI-module V(λ)⊆M(λ) with values V_{λ[n]} for n≥d and zero below d. Its generation degree is exactly d, weight is |λ|, injectivity degree is 0, and surjectivity and stability degrees are λ₁.

Over a commutative ring, pointwise tensor products of finitely generated FI-modules are finitely generated. If the factors are generated in degrees ≤m₁ and ≤m₂, their tensor product is generated in degree ≤m₁+m₂.
For each partition λ of size m, there is a rational character polynomial P_λ of weighted degree ≤m representing χ^{λ[n]} for every n≥m+λ₁ and every permutation in Sₙ.

For a finitely generated FI-module V over a characteristic-zero field with finite-dimensional values, weight d and stability degree s, there is a unique rational character polynomial of weighted degree ≤d representing χ_{Vₙ} for every n≥s+d.

concerns.concern: Source locator at items/def-fi-coinvariant-functors-and-transition-maps.md:30 describes CE​​FN Definition 2.4 and Lemma 2.5 as 'the same coinvariant quotient in the $H_0$ notation'. They concern a different functor: H₀(V)_S quotients V_S by images from smaller sets, whereas Φₐ quotients by moving-block group relations. For the constant free module M(0), H₀(M(0))ₙ=0 for n>0 but Φ₀(M(0))ₙ=k. Verified in [FI-modules over Noetherian rings](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~farb/papers/FImodNoetherian.pdf), Definition 2.4 and complete Lemma 2.5 proof, PDF page 11. The local Definition is sound; the secondary source description is inaccurate.

The secondary source locator at items/thm-finite-generation-is-equivalent-to-uniform-representation-stability.md:34 says 'Remark 1.2, printed p. 3: the same equivalence in the Noetherian-rings context'. Remark 1.2 discusses eventual character polynomiality in characteristic zero and a possible positive-characteristic Brauer-character analogue, rather than the stated equivalence. See [FI-modules over Noetherian rings](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~farb/papers/FImodNoetherian.pdf), Remark 1.2. The correctly cited [CEF Theorem 1.13 and its proof](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.4533) support the local theorem.

The secondary source locator at items/prop-weight-and-stability-degree-give-uniform-representation-stability-range.md:31 calls CE​​FN §1, printed pp. 1–2, 'the same stability-range statement'. Those pages mention representation stability but do not state the quantitative range n≥weight(V)+stab-deg(V). Checked the cited introductory pages in [FI-modules over Noetherian rings](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~farb/papers/FImodNoetherian.pdf). The local argument and primary [CEF Proposition 3.3.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.4533) do establish that range.

Verification 1.2, items/ex-exterior-square-of-the-fi-permutation-module.md:79, says the diagonal entry is '+1 exactly for the unordered pairs of distinct fixed points' and '−1 exactly for the 2-cycles'. The example permits characteristic 2, where these scalar values coincide. For k=F₂ and σ=(0 1), the only wedge has diagonal entry 1 although σ has no fixed points. The signed contribution calculation and final integer-valued trace formula remain correct; the 'exactly' classification needs qualification as an integral sign classification before mapping to k.

seams_checked.note: Opened both page texts and the padding Definition. Batch 18 uses λ[n] only at n≥|λ|+λ₁, preserves the empty-partition convention, and does not attribute FI transition maps or stability to the neutral padding Definition. No internal/outer-product conflation was found.

Opened the consumer page and thm-murnaghan-stability-for-kronecker-coefficients. F1–F3 and Proof 1.1–3.1 preserve the characteristic-zero, finite-dimensionality, padding-threshold and finite-generation hypotheses of the realization, tensor-product and representation-stability suppliers.
